GenerateMonsters.note: C# draws one NextItem over the 3-value SecondaryEnemyType enum (declaration order SnappingJaxfruit/MediumSlime/SmallSlimes) to pick a branch: SnappingJaxfruit costs 0 further draws (a fixed monster); MediumSlime costs 1 draw over _mediumSlimes ([Leaf,Twig]); SmallSlimes costs 2 draws over _smallSlimes -- WITH replacement (both NextItem calls read the same 2-element array with no removal, so duplicates are possible, e.g. two Leaf). Every branch appends SlitheringStrangler last. The sim's parity branch mirrors this exactly via a `pick()` helper wrapping selection_rng.next_item, including the with-replacement SmallSlimes double-draw (`secondary = [pick(smalls)(...), pick(smalls)(...)]`, no removal between the two). Executed witness (seed 12345): roster=['TwigSlimeM','SlitheringStrangler'], draws=2 -- the MediumSlime branch (1 secondary draw + 1 branch-select draw = 2), SlitheringStrangler always last. Draw count is correctly variable by branch (1 for SnappingJaxfruit, 2 for MediumSlime, 3 for SmallSlimes) in both C# and sim. See the guards entry below for the non-parity (legacy) path.

guards.what: Encounter Rng independence outside parity (default/legacy) mode
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `RunState.create_combat` now builds the per-encounter Rng on BOTH paths: with a string seed from `rng_set.seed` as before, and without one from a run seed derived at construction (`run.derive_encounter_seed`, a hash of the shared generator's STATE, so it consumes no draw and shifts no other legacy stream). `create_monsters`' `selection_rng=None` arm is therefore unreachable from any production call site, and the composition no longer moves when the shared stream does — executed in test/test_encounter_selection_rng.py (test_the_composition_does_not_move_with_the_shared_stream) and by audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py legacy-shared-stream.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Same mechanism as ruby_raiders' guard (full rationale there). With no string seed, SlitheringStranglerEncounter.create_monsters's `pick()` helper falls back to `rng.choice(items)` on the shared combat_rng.legacy() stream for the branch-select and the secondary-monster picks alike. Executed witness: py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py legacy-shared-stream confirms the shared-object identity for CombatState(encounter=SLITHERING_STRANGLER_NORMAL). Does not explain the 89U conformance divergence (89U's replay takes the correct parity branch, verdicted faithful above).
